description: Columnar storage + vectorized execution decomposed. ClickHouse, DuckDB, Snowflake, BigQuery, Spark all use this. SIMD on columns, compression cascades, late materialisation, vectorized operators, columnar joins.

sub_mechanisms.name: row_vs_column_layout
sub_mechanisms.definition: Row: row1_col1 row1_col2 row1_col3 row2_col1 ... Column: col1_row1 col1_row2 col2_row1 col2_row2 ...
sub_mechanisms.why: Row format: read whole row. Column: read only needed columns. For analytical queries scanning few columns over many rows, column layout reduces I/O proportionally.

sub_mechanisms.name: SIMD_on_columns
sub_mechanisms.definition: Per-column dense layout → vectorisable. Add two columns: process 8 floats per AVX-256 instruction.
sub_mechanisms.why: Row format: integer column scattered among other types — no SIMD. Column format: contiguous floats → SIMD-friendly. ClickHouse uses heavily.

sub_mechanisms.name: column_compression
sub_mechanisms.definition: Similar values together compress better. Sorted column with run-length encoding can shrink dramatically.
sub_mechanisms.why: Same data; better compression. Combined with dictionary, RLE, bit-pack: 5-10x size reduction over row format. Foundation of OLAP storage economics.

sub_mechanisms.name: late_materialisation
sub_mechanisms.definition: Postpone reconstructing rows as long as possible. Operate on columns; assemble rows only at result.
sub_mechanisms.why: Avoid building tuples that get filtered out. Filter + aggregation done on columns; final result materialised once. Combined with vectorisation gives 10-100x speedup.

sub_mechanisms.name: vectorized_filter_operator
sub_mechanisms.definition: Process N-row batch: scalar predicate evaluated on N values; produces selection bitmap.
sub_mechanisms.why: Per-row: branch + check per iteration. Vectorised: SIMD evaluates 8 at once → 8x speedup. Bitmap drives subsequent operators.

sub_mechanisms.name: vectorized_aggregation
sub_mechanisms.definition: SUM, AVG, MIN, MAX computed over batch. SIMD reduction across N values.
sub_mechanisms.why: Hot OLAP operator. SIMD reduction in a few cycles per N values. ClickHouse + DuckDB get massive aggregate query speedups.

sub_mechanisms.name: vectorized_hash_join
sub_mechanisms.definition: Build phase: hash all build-side rows in vectorized batches. Probe phase: compute hashes for batch of probe rows; lookup; collect matches.
sub_mechanisms.why: Per-row: hash + lookup per iteration. Vectorised: prefetch hash table entries; batched lookups; fewer cache misses. 5-10x faster than scalar.

sub_mechanisms.name: selection_vector
sub_mechanisms.definition: Bitmap or integer array indicating which positions in a batch are 'alive' (passed filters).
sub_mechanisms.why: Avoid copying after filter. Subsequent operators apply only to alive positions. Standard mechanism in vectorized engines.

sub_mechanisms.name: ClickHouse_MergeTree
sub_mechanisms.definition: ClickHouse's storage engine: columnar parts + background merges. LSM-like for OLAP.
sub_mechanisms.why: ORDER BY clause defines part organisation. Inserts go to small parts; merges combine. Read paths efficiently leverage sort order.

sub_mechanisms.name: predicate_pushdown_columnar
sub_mechanisms.definition: Filter applied as early as possible; combined with column stats to skip blocks.
sub_mechanisms.why: Same as Parquet predicate pushdown but in execution context. Engine reads block stats; skips if filter incompatible; evaluates filter vectorized on surviving blocks.

sub_mechanisms.name: MPP_massively_parallel_processing
sub_mechanisms.definition: Distributed OLAP: data sharded across nodes; queries execute in parallel; results merged.
sub_mechanisms.why: Foundation of Snowflake, BigQuery, Redshift, Spark SQL. Combine columnar within node with parallelism across nodes. Critical for petabyte-scale.

sub_mechanisms.name: shuffle_in_distributed_columnar
sub_mechanisms.definition: Redistribute data across nodes for join or aggregation. Hash partition by join key.
sub_mechanisms.why: Distributed join needs both sides' matching rows on same node. Shuffle = network-cost expensive operation. Query optimizer minimises shuffles (e.g., broadcast small side).

derivation_rules.name: columnar_layout_wins_for_analytical_queries
if: query scans large data but uses few columns
then: columnar layout reduces I/O proportionally to columns-used / columns-total
derivation_rules.why: SELECT sum(amount) FROM 1B-row table with 50 columns: row = read 1B × 50 columns; column = read 1B × 1 column. 50x less I/O. Standard OLAP advantage over row stores.

derivation_rules.name: vectorized_execution_amortises_per_call_overhead
if: operator processes batches of N rows per call
then: per-row call/dispatch overhead is amortised across N rows
derivation_rules.why: Volcano per-row: ~10ns dispatch + ~10ns work = 20ns/row. Vectorised per-N: ~10ns dispatch + N × 1-2ns work. For N=1024: ~1ns/row. 20x speedup before SIMD.

derivation_rules.name: SIMD_compounds_vectorized_speedup
then: per-row cost drops further by SIMD width factor
derivation_rules.why: AVX-256: 8 floats per instruction. Vectorized + SIMD: 1ns/row → 0.125ns/row. Total speedup over Volcano: 100x+. Critical for OLAP query latency.

derivation_rules.name: row_storage_OLTP_columnar_OLAP
derivation_rules.why: Update row in columnar: touch many columns = many seeks. In row: one write. OLTP needs row. OLAP scans columns, gets compression bonus, wants columnar. Different stores for different workloads.

derivation_rules.name: MPP_shuffle_minimisation_dominates_distributed_perf
derivation_rules.why: Shuffle = network transfer across nodes. Far slower than local compute. Optimisers go to lengths to avoid (broadcast small joins, push aggregations down, partition tables to avoid shuffle). Single biggest distributed-query optimisation.
